app.tagline: Replay analyzer for World of Tanks and Mir Tankov
upload.drop: Drop a .wotreplay or .mtreplay here, or click to browse
upload.local: Parsed on your computer. Nothing is uploaded.
report.subject: Player
report.subjectPartial: Numbers for other players are partial: the replay only saw what the recorder's side could see, so damage taken and unspotted positions are incomplete.
report.partial: Partially supported version: positions, shots, damage and results are read. Kills are rebuilt from the results (time within half a second), and hits on tanks the recorder could not see are missing, so some numbers are less reliable here.
parser.partialSupport: Methods were guessed from payload shapes because this version has no manifest: damage, kills and positions are decoded, but some methods are unrecognized, so some numbers may be incomplete.
col.name: Player
adv.title: Beyond classic stats
adv.sub: Weighted by who you were fighting and by how the battle stood
adv.dpm.tip: Damage ÷ minutes you were alive. Classic trackers use damage per battle.
adv.threat.tip: Each hit counts more when the target was dangerous: its own damage per minute vs the enemy team's median (1.0 = average target, capped 0.25–3).
adv.onthreats.tip: Share of your damage that went to enemies out-damaging the enemy median.
adv.impact.tip: Sum of the change in your team's win probability caused by your hits. Win probability v0 = remaining HP and tank count (initial model, will be calibrated).
adv.cleanup.tip: Share of your damage dealt after your team was already ≥ 90% to win.
viz.wp.sub: your team's chance over battle time (v0, uncalibrated)
viz.wp.aria: Line chart of your team's win probability over battle time with kill markers
viz.impact.sub: win-probability points each hit moved, and the running total
viz.impact.aria: Bars of win probability change per hit with cumulative line
viz.targets.sub: bar = raw damage, notch = weighted by how dangerous the target was
viz.targets.aria: Bar chart of damage by target
fb.note: Votes stay in this browser; nothing is uploaded. Copy them to send to us.
viz.cmp.sub: the same measure for all players
viz.cmp.aria: Bar chart comparing the selected measure across all players
viz.cmp.note: Dashed bars with ~ are partial: the replay only records hits that happened where the recorder could see, so we saw under 75% of that player's damage. Win-probability swing for others is measured from their own team's side.
gl.aimsame.how: We estimate each turret direction every 2 s from the shots (see Aim). For each pair of players alive at the same time, we count the samples where the two turrets point within 20 degrees of each other. Shown as that share.
gl.aimsame.mean: High means the two were aiming at the same things, like focus fire or a pair working together. Low means they were looking elsewhere. Turret directions are estimates until gun data exists, so read it as a pattern.
viz.aim.sub: how often each player aimed the same way as the one you pick
viz.aim.aria: Bar chart of how often each player aimed the same way as the picked player
gl.reloadspin.how: From the shots each tank fired, we average the gap between bursts over the battle (the reload). The spinner shows how far through that reload the gun is, from the last burst. Shown only while reloading.
gl.reloadspin.mean: It is an estimate from the replay, not the game's own reload timer. Use it to see when a tank was exposed while its gun was empty.
gl.aimteam.how: Same as the pair view, for a whole side: each member's share of samples where their turret is within 20 degrees of each other member's, averaged over the side. The top line is the average over every pair on that side.
gl.aimteam.mean: High means the side moves and aims as one group. Low means its players fight on their own. Compare the two sides: a coherent enemy team is a target for focus fire.
viz.dist.sub: Pick players: each gets a coloured line at their value and a percentile among all players in the battle.
viz.dist.aria: Distribution of the metric across all players, with a coloured line per picked player
fb.note.cloud: Votes are anonymous: only the metric ids and 👍/👎 are sent, never your replay or names.
fb.fail: Couldn't reach the server; use Copy instead.
err.crash: Something went wrong showing this page.
adv.bold.tip: Of the moments you could have fought (visible enemy within 220 m, game still open, gun probably ready), how many you took by firing within 5 s. High = you take chances; low = you sit them out. Not a verdict: some roles should wait.
gl.impact.how: We rebuild your team's win chance every second from the tanks alive and their HP (model v0). For each of your hits we take the win chance just after minus just before, and add them up, in percentage points.
gl.impact.mean: Positive means your hits moved the game your team's way. It rewards damage that came when the result was open. The model is uncalibrated, so use it to compare players within one battle, not across battles.
gl.threat.how: Each of your hits counts as damage × target weight. The weight is the target's damage per minute divided by the enemy team's median, limited to 0.25–3. Summed over all your hits.
gl.threat.mean: Above your raw damage means you hit the dangerous players; below means much of it went on weak ones. ×1.00 is an average target.
gl.onthreats.how: Share of your damage that landed on enemies with weight 1.0 or higher (they out-damaged the enemy median).
gl.onthreats.mean: High means your shots went to the tanks that hurt your team most.
gl.cleanup.how: Share of your damage dealt while your team's win chance was already 90% or more.
gl.cleanup.mean: High means a lot of your damage came after the result was mostly decided. Classic stats count it in full; we show it separately.
gl.dpm.how: Damage dealt ÷ minutes you were alive (at least 10 seconds). Lifetime comes from the battle results.
gl.dpm.mean: Fair for short and long lives alike. Classic trackers use damage per battle, which hides how quickly you worked.
gl.bold.how: We check every second you were alive and visible. An opening is a second with an enemy visible within 220 m, the game still open (your team below 90% to win) and your gun probably ready (estimated from your own fastest shot cycle). Openings close together form one episode. Initiative = episodes where you fired within 5 s ÷ all episodes. Needs at least 3 episodes.
gl.bold.mean: High means you take chances when they exist; low means you wait them out. Neither is wrong on its own: some roles should wait. Read it together with how the chances went.
gl.paid.how: For each chance you took we look from its start to 5 s after its end. It paid off if the damage you dealt there (each hit × target weight) was at least what you lost, or you got a kill. Shown as a share of the chances you took; needs at least 3.
gl.paid.mean: High means that when you commit, you win the exchange.
gl.costly.how: A taken chance is costly if, in that window, you lost at least 10% of your max HP, dealt less (target-weighted) than you lost, and got no kill. Shown as a share of the chances you took; needs at least 3.
gl.costly.mean: High means you often commit into exchanges you lose. The fix is usually the moment (reload, cover, support), not fighting less.
gl.style.how: Safe: initiative under 35%. Bold and costly: initiative 35% or more and 40% or more of taken chances were costly. Bold and rewarded: initiative 60% or more, under 40% costly and 50% or more paid off. Anything else: balanced.
gl.style.mean: A description of how you played this battle, not a grade. The thresholds are first guesses and will be recalibrated on real battles.
gl.acc.how: Hits ÷ shots from the battle results.
gl.acc.mean: Low accuracy costs damage. Big or close targets inflate it, so compare with similar tanks.
gl.pen.how: Penetrating hits ÷ hits from the battle results.
gl.pen.mean: Low means many shots met armour. Look at ammo choice and aiming points.
gl.life.how: Your time alive ÷ battle length, both from the battle results.
gl.life.mean: 100% means you survived to the end. Surviving is not a goal by itself: read it next to damage and Impact.
player.timeline: Timeline: win chance curve and kills
player.nomap: Grid only: map image arrives with game data
coach.title: Coach
coach.sub: Moments worth a look, with what they cost
coach.none: No moments above the confidence bar in this battle ({n} checks run). That is a result, not a gap: the detectors are few and still growing.
coach.earlyHpDump.title: Lost {pct}% of your HP in the first two minutes
coach.earlyHpDump.body: {hp} HP went to {by} enemy tank(s) before 2:00.
coach.earlyHpDump.fix: Open from a safer spot and let the first shots come to you: the opening exchange rarely decides the game.
coach.isolatedUnderFire.title: Alone under fire
coach.isolatedUnderFire.body: Your nearest ally was {dist} m away, {enemies} enemies were in view and you took {hp} HP.
coach.isolatedUnderFire.fix: Fall back toward your team before the fight, or wait until an ally is within about 120 m.
coach.collision.good.title: Good ram
coach.collision.good.body: You rammed an enemy and dealt {dealt} while taking {got}.
coach.collision.good.fix: Ramming works when it wins the contact. Repeat it when the enemy is weakened and you are not.
coach.collision.title: Rammed a teammate
coach.collision.body: Contact damage: you dealt {dealt} and took {got}. Nothing was gained, the team just lost HP.
coach.collision.fix: Check the tank beside you before you turn or reverse. A collision with an ally is never a trade.
coach.badTrade.title: Lost the exchange
coach.badTrade.body: You started it, dealt {dealt} and took {got}.
coach.badTrade.fix: Start exchanges from cover or with an ally covering, and leave once the trade turns against you.
coach.wonTrade.title: Won the exchange
coach.wonTrade.fix: This is the pattern to repeat.
coach.idleWithTargets.title: Idle with enemies in view
coach.idleWithTargets.body: {secs} s without a shot or real movement while an enemy was visible nearby. At your own average pace that is about {dmg} damage.
coach.idleWithTargets.fix: Take a spot where you can shoot, or move to where the fight is.
coach.deathRecap.title: How you died
coach.deathRecap.body: In the last {secs} s you lost {lost} HP from {sources} source(s), most from {main} ({mainHp}). Killed by {killer}. Nearest ally: {ally}.
coach.deathRecap.fix: Look at where you stood in the seconds before: who could see you and from where.
coach.survivedUnusedHp.title: Survived with HP to spare
coach.survivedUnusedHp.body: Your team lost; you finished with {hp} HP and dealt {dealt} damage.
coach.survivedUnusedHp.fix: When the game is slipping, trade HP for damage earlier: unused HP wins nothing.
coach.lowYieldClip.title: Low-yield clip
coach.lowYieldClip.body: Clip of {shells} shells: {pens} penetrated for {dmg} damage.
coach.lowYieldClip.fix: Against armour you cannot penetrate, a full clip is wasted: switch target or reposition before you empty it.
coach.lowYieldSummary.title: Clip economy
coach.lowYieldSummary.body: {lowN} clips ({lowShells} shells) did {lowDmg} damage; the other {highN} ({highShells} shells) did {highDmg}.
coach.lowYieldSummary.fix: Aim clips at targets you can penetrate: the weak half of your clips is where the damage went missing.
coach.shootingOnTheMove.title: Shooting on the move
coach.shootingOnTheMove.body: {fast} of {total} shots were fired above 20 km/h, and only {penRate}% of them penned.
coach.shootingOnTheMove.fix: Stop or slow below 20 km/h before firing.
coach.punishedReload.title: Punished a reload
coach.punishedReload.body: Hit {enemy} for {dmg} damage while they were reloading.
coach.punishedReload.fix: Keep pressure on reloading enemies: every shell into a reload is damage they can't answer.
coach.exposedWhileReloading.title: Exposed while reloading
coach.exposedWhileReloading.body: Took {dmg} damage while reloading, having moved only {moved} m since your last shot.
coach.exposedWhileReloading.fix: After you shoot, keep moving: a stationary reload is a free target — pull back toward cover before the reload ends.
coach.peekIntoLoadedAutoloader.title: Peeked a loaded autoloader
coach.peekIntoLoadedAutoloader.body: You peeked {enemy} right after it reloaded and took {got} HP.
coach.peekIntoLoadedAutoloader.fix: Count its reload from its last shot and peek while it is still reloading, not after.
map.title: Map image for {name}
map.help: Optional. Use the minimap picture and the arena XML from your own game files. They stay on this device and are never uploaded.
map.noxml: No boundingBox found in that file; type the four numbers (metres).
map.invalid: Choose an image and enter valid bounds (x0 < x1, z0 < z1).
map.savefail: Could not save in this browser.
curve.aria: Running metric over the battle, synced with the replay
curve.partial: Hits seen for this player cover {p}% of their official damage, so the curve ends low.
curve.wp.how: Team win probability (v0). Rises when your side trades well. Findings are marked with dashed lines.
curve.dmg.how: Damage dealt to enemies so far, summed from observed hits. Flat stretches are time without hitting anything.
curve.dpm.how: Damage so far ÷ minutes of battle (or of life, once destroyed). Shows if you are ahead of or behind your usual pace now.
curve.hit.how: Damaging hits ÷ shots so far (needs 3 shots). Shots that bounce or miss count as not damaging, so this is below the official accuracy. It settles as shots pile up.
mp.aria: Heatmap of the battle on the map
mp.legend: Darkest cell = {max} · cell {cell} m · total {total}. Tap a cell to read it; pinch, wheel or +/− to zoom, drag to pan.
mp.agg: Win rate by spawn side and other all-battle statistics need many battles. They appear here once opt-in aggregates exist; this page shows only the battles you load.
mp.l.presence.how: Each second a tank is alive adds one second to the map cell it stands in. Enemies count only where we actually saw them.
mp.l.presence.mean: Where fights and lanes really are, and where your team spent its time.
mp.l.dmgdealt.how: Each damaging hit adds its damage to the cell where the target stood.
mp.l.dmgdealt.mean: Where damage is won. Compare your hot cells with the team's.
mp.l.dmgrecv.how: Each damaging hit adds its damage to the cell where the victim stood.
mp.l.dmgrecv.mean: Where tanks get hurt. Bright cells on your own path are places to avoid or to approach differently.
mp.l.deaths.how: Each destroyed tank adds 1 to the cell where it died.
mp.l.deaths.mean: Positions that cost lives. Repeated deaths in one spot suggest a trap.
mp.l.routes.how: Presence limited to the first 60 seconds of the battle.
mp.l.routes.mean: Which lanes each side takes at the start.
mp.l.spots.how: The first time an enemy was spotted, we add 1 to the cell where it stood.
mp.l.spots.mean: Where enemies get found. Bright cells on the way to your position are where you are first seen.
mp.l.tracers.how: One line per shot: from where the shooter stood when firing to where the shell ended (hit, ricochet or ground). Blue = your team, red = enemy. We see an end point for about three quarters of shots.
mp.l.tracers.mean: Which lanes are shot across, from where, and how far. Many lines crossing your position mean a hot firing lane. Long lines from one spot show a sniping position.
mp.tracers.legend: {n} shots with a known end point. Blue = your team, red = enemy.
log.title: Damage log
log.empty: No damage events for this filter.
log.note: Hits as recorded in the replay; ☠ = destroyed. Click a row to jump 3 s before it.
log.coverage: The log holds {p}% of the damage in the official results (the replay only reports hits it could see).
gl.focus.how: Of the damage you dealt, the share on targets that a teammate also hit within 4 s before or after. Needs at least 3 hits. Only hits the replay reports are counted.
gl.focus.mean: High means you and your team break targets together, so enemies die before they can trade back. Low means you shoot different targets, or alone. A sniper on a far lane can be low and still useful.
gl.company.how: Of your damaging hits, the share fired while a living teammate stood within 150 m of you. Needs at least 3 hits.
gl.company.mean: High means you fight next to teammates who can cover you or finish the exchange. Low means you were the lone wolf. Low is a risk if you were alone under fire, and fine on a flank that the team agreed to hold.
gl.hang.how: We count each second you were alive and in the rearmost third of your living team (by distance travelled from the spawn), while a teammate was taking damage within the last 5 s and you had not fired within 5 s either side. Shown as seconds and as a share of your time alive.
gl.hang.mean: Seconds in which teammates were fighting up front while you stayed behind and did nothing. Some of it is right (holding a lane, waiting for the reload), so check each moment before changing your play.
gl.rank.how: Every second you are alive we rank you among your living teammates by how far each has moved from the team's spawn point, 0% = last, 100% = furthest forward, then average. Needs the team's spawn positions.
gl.rank.mean: Low means you tend to trail the team, high means you lead the push. Neither is a verdict: heavy tanks usually lead and snipers trail. It becomes useful together with Hung back and Fought with company.
gl.spread.how: Every 5 s we take your living teammates, find their centre, and average how far each stands from it (metres). The value shown is the average over the battle.
gl.spread.mean: Small means the team stayed together, large means it was strung out over the map. A team that fights as one blob wins local fights; a very spread team is easier to pick apart, but some maps need it.
crew.absorbed: teammates absorbed {hp} HP from the same enemies
crew.lowcov: we see only {p}% of this player's damage, so this is less certain
crew.legend: Dots under the line: blue = teammates' good plays, red = enemies'. A ring means teammates made it possible. A cross is a heavy losing exchange (danger spot). Faded = we see little of that player. Tap a mark to jump to it.
adv.enabled: Your good plays enabled by teammates
gl.align.how: We find every won trade by your teammates (the same rule as your own good plays: enough damage dealt and a good damage ratio). A play counts as aligned when a different teammate made a good play within 10 s of it. Shown as the share of aligned plays and the counts. Needs at least 2 plays.
gl.align.mean: High means your team's strong moments happen together, which is what coordinated pushes and focus fire look like. Low means good plays were scattered. Small counts are noisy, and we only see the hits the replay reports.
gl.enabled.how: For each of your good plays we look at the enemies you traded with. If, in the 15 s before and during the play, those enemies hit teammates for at least as much as they hit you, or destroyed a teammate, the play counts as enabled by teammates. Shown as plays enabled ÷ all your good plays.
gl.enabled.mean: Enabled means teammates drew the fire that let you win the trade. That is teamplay, not luck. Not enabled means you won it on your own. We cannot separate luck yet because that needs gun data (damage range, penetration).
led.title: Sacrifice ledger (your team)
led.made.tip: Teammates' good plays in which this player absorbed fire from the same enemies or was destroyed by them
led.cashed.tip: This player's own good plays that teammates made possible, out of all their good plays
gl.ledger.how: For every good play by a teammate (a won trade), we look at the enemies that teammate traded with. Players who took damage from those enemies in the 15 s before and during the play, or were destroyed by them, are credited with 'made space for'. HP absorbed adds up that damage. 'Own plays enabled' counts this player's own good plays that were carried by teammates (see Your good plays enabled by teammates).
gl.ledger.mean: It shows who creates space for others and who cashes in. A player with many 'made space' and few own plays took the hits so others could shoot. Taking hits is not automatically good: it only counts when a teammate then won a trade. Small numbers are noisy and we only see the hits the replay reports.
curve.flank.none: Not enough tracked positions to find the attack axis in this replay.
curve.flank.how: The map is split into left, centre and right (looking from your spawn toward the enemy). Each strip shows, every 5 s, who has more HP on that flank among tanks we can see: blue = your team ahead, red = behind, grey = about even, empty = nobody much there. Enemies count only while seen.
gl.reinforce.how: A flank counts as being lost when your team's share of the HP we can see there stays below 40% for 15 s. For each such episode we check whether any teammate who started on another flank reached it within 30 s. Shown as episodes answered / episodes, and the typical (median) time to arrive.
gl.reinforce.mean: A team that answers a losing flank quickly keeps fights even. Low means flanks were left to fend for themselves. Remember that enemies only count while seen, and some losing flanks cannot be helped in time.
gl.reinforced.how: How many of those flank episodes you answered: you started on another flank and reached the losing one within 30 s, and you were alive.
gl.reinforced.mean: Shows whether you move toward trouble. 0 is fine when your own flank was the one in danger or no episode needed you, so read it with the team value.
cov.title: Data coverage
cov.how: Damage = hits the replay reports ÷ official damage of all players. Shots = shot events ÷ official shots (can pass 100%). Positions = share of alive time with a known position. Good = at least 85% of damage and the enemy seen for 40% of their time; low = under 50% of damage.
cov.mean: The replay only sends what the recorder's client knew, so other players' numbers are partial and enemy positions only exist while they were visible. Low coverage does not make a number wrong, but trust team-wide and enemy values less, and the coach is more careful there.
dg.title: Danger spots (worst moment per player)
dg.none: No heavy losing exchanges found for this side.
dg.do.alone: Don't stand more than ~120 m from your nearest ally: nobody splits the incoming fire or finishes the shooter.
dg.do.crossfire: Don't show yourself to two or more enemies at once: you can only trade with one, the rest hit for free. Peek from where one enemy can see you.
dg.do.early: Don't take the first minute's contact with a big HP loss: HP is the budget for the whole fight. Let the other side commit first.
dg.do.outtraded: Don't keep trading when you lose the exchange: back out after the first bad hits and re-peek when the enemy reloads.
gl.danger.how: The same rule as the bad-trade detector, applied to every player: an engagement (hits within 8 s) where the player received at least 25% of max HP and dealt less than half of that. The cause is the first that fits: Alone (nearest living ally farther than 120 m at the start), Crossfire (two or more different enemies hit them), Opening (before 1:00), otherwise Out-traded. We show each player's worst engagement.
gl.danger.mean: It points at the moment and the likely reason, not at a verdict. Hits on players the recording did not see are missing, so other players' numbers can be too low, and the thresholds are first guesses.
report.mode: This is not a 15v15 random battle. Win probability, trades and teamplay numbers assume 15v15 random, so treat them as rough.
mp.l.danger.how: Each player's heavy losing exchanges (the Danger spots table in the report) are placed at the cell where that player stood when the exchange began.
mp.l.danger.mean: Where players lose fights they should not take. Bright cells are places many players got hurt; a bright cell on your own side is a spot to avoid or cover with a teammate.
adv.support.tip: Assisted damage (spotting, tracks, stuns) per minute alive, and its share of damage dealt plus assisted
gl.support.how: Assisted damage from the battle results: damage your teammates did to enemies you spotted (radio), tracked or stunned. We divide it by the minutes you were alive. The share is assisted ÷ (assisted + your own damage).
gl.support.mean: Scouts and support tanks create damage that never shows in their own damage. A high share means your value came from enabling others. We cannot yet say which spots led to which damage, or how good each spot was.
mv.title: Movement and exposure (your team)
mv.multi.tip: Share of visible time with at least two enemy tanks within 150 m
mv.acq.tip: Median seconds from a new enemy contact (none within 150 m for 10 s before) to your next shot
gl.movement.how: Once per second we take every tank we can see. Speed is metres travelled per minute, standing still is the share of seconds under 1 m/s. Exposure is the share of seconds with two or more living enemies within 150 m. Time to first shot is the median wait from a new contact (no enemy within 150 m for 10 s) to that player's next shot, ignoring waits over 20 s.
gl.movement.mean: A very mobile player who is rarely under several enemies is probably working flanks; a high exposure share is the daredevil pattern that the danger spots table punishes. A slow first shot after contact may be hesitation or reload, we cannot tell yet. Enemy positions are known only while spotted, so compare players of the same team only. No line of sight yet, so 'within 150 m' can include enemies behind cover.
pov.note: Simple 3D: drag to look around, wheel or pinch to zoom, double-click to reset. Flat ground, boxes for tanks; trees, bushes, clouds and mountains are decoration only and do not show real cover. Yellow = enemy that hit the followed tank in the last 4 s. Turret direction and the aim counter are estimates: the turret points along each shell's path and turns at an assumed 30°/s; aim time is an assumed 2.3 s (typical medium gun). Real values need gun data. In first person the view zooms in automatically (scope) while the shooter is estimated to be aimed at a target.
mp.l.vanish.how: Each time an enemy tank that is still alive leaves our team's vision, it is counted in the cell where it was last seen. Short flickers and deaths are left out.
mp.l.vanish.mean: A clue to cover and line-of-sight breaks: places where enemies keep disappearing are likely behind something or in foliage. It can also be camouflage, range or a spotter that died, so one replay is weak evidence; many replays on the same map would make it reliable.
pause.title: Pause options
pov.resync.tip: Return the camera to the replayed player's own view direction
player.heights.note: Estimated from where tanks drove. Solid = tanks were there, hatched = guessed. Not cover.
ui.more: How we get it and what it means
style.title: Style and score
style.sub: Each player against their team. 100 = team average. Percentages are the share of the team average.
style.score.tip: Team-relative iVi-like score: weighted average of the inputs, team average = 100.
style.pressure.tip: Brave/PVS shape: damage per minute × (shifted exchange)^1.5, relative to the team average (1.00 = average).
style.note: v0: weights and the slope proxy are initial guesses in packages/analysis/config/style-v0.json. Not a replacement for the in-game iVi.
style.col.skillDpm.tip: Damage per minute with each hit weighted by the target's skill (style score), vs team average. Separate from the score.
style.col.dpm.tip: Damage per minute vs team average
style.col.kpm.tip: Kills per minute vs team average
style.col.exchange.tip: Damage dealt ÷ damage received vs team average
style.col.mPerMin.tip: Metres moved per minute vs team average
style.col.stillShare.tip: Share of time standing still vs team average
style.col.survival.tip: Share of the battle alive vs team average
style.col.spottedPerMin.tip: Spotted enemies per minute vs team average
style.col.assistsPerMin.tip: Assist damage per minute vs team average
style.col.boldRate.tip: Share of bold chances taken vs team average
style.col.focusShare.tip: Share of hits on the same target as the team vs team average
